hook: Ian T. Jolliffe is a British statistician who completed his PhD at the University of Sussex before building his academic career at the University of Aberdeen, where he became a professor of statistics. He worked extensively on principal component analysis, a method for reducing the number of variables in a dataset while preserving as much of its variability as possible. In 1986 he published the first edition of his textbook Principal Component Analysis, which organized and extended the scattered literature on the technique into a single reference. A substantially expanded second edition followed in 2002, nearly doubling the material and adding coverage of newer variants and applications. His textbook became the standard reference work for the method across statistics, and PCA itself became one of the most widely used tools for dimensionality reduction in modern data analysis and machine learning. He is also a member of the American Statistical Association.
